column5: The browser's speech rate is fixed at 1.25 today and screen-reader users differ widely in the rate they want.
column6: The rationale names only screen-reader users, who often like fast speech. 고령층 and 결혼이민자 likely need speech slower than 1.25, which makes A3 more urgent than this plan says.
column7: 근거를 '사람마다 원하는 속도가 다르고 고령층·결혼이민자는 더 느린 말이 필요'로 고치고, 기본 속도 1.25 재검토를 A3에 넣는다.

column5: Hidden text is where a page can plant instructions that no sighted helper would ever notice

column5: Text written for screen readers (visually clipped, not `display: none`) stays, because it is written for our users.
column6: Dated plan. It equates 'our users' with screen-reader users. Keeping sr-only text is still fine, but the users are now 정보취약계층 broadly.
column7: 기록으로 둔다. 다시 쓸 때는 'written for screen-reader users, one of our groups'.

column5: Clicks are then reported correctly, but the agent keeps reading text a sighted person cannot see.
column6: This option was built (line 27): mainText keeps CSS-hidden menus and tab panels for reading. A sighted older adult who follows on screen hears text they cannot find there.

column5: for a blind user who speaks Korean to it?

column7: 기록으로 둔다. 다시 쓸 때는 'for a 정보취약계층 user who speaks to it'.

column5: Keep structured text as the main sense. It is cheaper, it is what a screen reader user's world is made of
column6: Dated note. It justifies text-only perception by the screen-reader user's world, and the user is no longer only a screen-reader user.
column7: 기록으로 둔다. 근거에서 'screen reader user's world'를 빼거나 '시각장애 사용자에게는'으로 한정.

column5: Add a screenshot only as a fallback reader (stage 3).
column6: The built design keeps text-only perception, so it cannot resolve what sighted users point at: '빨간 버튼', '오른쪽 위에 있는 거', a picture. 고령층 who look at the screen often describe things by looks.
column7: 색·위치·그림으로 가리키는 말을 받을지 결정하고, 사진 설명 계획(core/picture.py)과 함께 검토.
